public_rationale: On January 18, 2026, OpenAI's CFO described using lower-cost infrastructure for high-volume workloads when efficiency mattered more than raw scale [e9]. This disclosure predates the March 3 statement and identifies a concrete cost-management strategy beyond revenue growth [e9]. It contradicts the categorical claim that OpenAI had no such plan [e9].
limitations: The company disclosure does not independently verify execution or establish that the strategy can deliver sustainable profitability [e9].
This evidence does not establish what plans OpenAI's peers had [e9].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and its peers have no plan for making AI economics work beyond projecting that revenue will keep growing.

statement.excerpt: However, the way that OpenAI describes the AI industry sure does sound like a scam. It’s very obvious that neither OpenAI nor its peers have any plan to make any of this work beyond saying “well we’ll just keep making more money,” and I’m being quite literal, per The Information:
statement.document_title: The AI Bubble Is An Information War

from_speaker: neither OpenAI nor its peers have any plan
beyond saying “well we’ll just keep making more money”
our_interpretation: Assess the existence of economic strategies, not whether those strategies will succeed.
The plain reading excludes a concrete plan to improve economics through cost control, efficiency, or capital discipline beyond revenue growth.
Treat 'sounds like a scam' as commentary, not a separate allegation of legally established fraud.
Use 2026 through publication as the current planning period. Earlier plans disclosed during this period qualify; strategies first adopted after publication do not.
A concrete OpenAI strategy beyond revenue growth is sufficient to contradict the categorical 'neither' assertion.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable evidence of the relevant plans establishes that they rely solely on rising revenue, with no concrete strategy addressing costs, efficiency, margins, or capital exposure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A plan in existence before publication specifies concrete economic measures beyond increasing revenue at OpenAI or a covered peer.

evidence.excerpt: We serve high-volume workloads on lower-cost infrastructure
evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'This turns compute from a fixed constraint'; later paragraph beginning 'This system requires discipline'
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's CFO described allocating workloads to cheaper infrastructure, partnering instead of owning, flexible contracts, and capital commitments tied to demand signals. These are stated cost and capital-management strategies beyond projecting revenue growth.
